terms.definition: A measure of the disorder of a system.
terms.examiner: Gases have much higher entropy than liquids or solids; more moles of gas in the products means ΔS(system) is positive.

terms.definition: ΔS(system) = sum of the entropies of the products − sum of the entropies of the reactants.
terms.examiner: Multiply each entropy by the number in the balanced equation.
Convert ΔH to J mol⁻¹, or ΔS to kJ, so the units match. T is in kelvin.
A reaction is feasible when ΔS(total) is positive.

terms.definition: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS(system). A reaction is feasible when ΔG is zero or negative.
terms.examiner: Feasible does not mean fast: a high activation energy can stop a feasible reaction from being seen.

terms.term: Free energy and the equilibrium constant
terms.examiner: A large negative ΔG gives a large K, so the equilibrium lies well to the right.
